section_1.title: Prerequisite: The Nature of Wave Interference
section_1.content: Briefly review the principle of superposition. Explain how two coherent light waves (same frequency, constant phase) meet to form an interference pattern of constructive and destructive peaks.
section_1.example: Visualizing two stones dropped in a pond: how their circular ripples overlap to create a stationary pattern of 'highs' and 'lows'.

section_2.title: The Mechanism of Diffraction
section_2.content: Explain Huygens-Fresnel principle. Diffraction occurs when light encounters an obstacle or aperture, causing it to spread out. Introduce the concept of a diffraction grating as a tool to map spatial information.
section_2.example: A laser pointer shining through a thin slit, creating a spread-out pattern of dots on a wall, where the distance between dots relates to the slit width.

section_3.title: Holography: Recording the Wavefront
section_3.content: Differentiate between photography (records intensity/amplitude only) and holography (records phase and amplitude). Show the 'reference beam' vs. the 'object beam' interference pattern recorded on a plate.
section_3.example: An 'Optic Spy Camera' that records not just a 2D image, but the complex 'echo' of light waves bouncing off a 3D object.

section_4.title: Reconstruction: The Diffraction Gate
section_4.content: Explain that the hologram acts as a complex diffraction grating. When the reference light hits the plate, it is diffracted by the microscopic interference patterns to reconstruct the original 3D wavefront.
section_4.example: A holographic 'Cyber-Pet' emerging from a flat card; when light hits the card, the diffraction pattern 'unfolds' the light into a 3D creature floating in mid-air.

section_5.title: Summary and Real-world Application
section_5.content: Synthesize how diffraction and interference enable data storage and 3D imaging. Conclude with the importance of coherent light (lasers) in this process.
section_5.example: Banknote security features: tilting a bill to see the color-shifting diffraction pattern that proves the holographic authenticity of the currency.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.3).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.0 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.2 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        lecture_lines = [
            "Holograms function as complex diffraction gratings.",

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
